name: Motorcycle
description: A road-registered motor vehicle with no more than three wheels on the ground, a straddle seat or standing platform, and handlebars. An electric one is a motorcycle when its motor exceeds 3,700 watts, or at any power when its seat is under 26 inches high, since neither fits the motor-driven cycle definition.

restrictions.rule: A motor vehicle with no more than three wheels on the ground, a saddle the rider straddles or a platform the rider stands on, and handlebars; not a motor-driven cycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter

An electric bike that fails the e-bike definition is a motorcycle when its motor exceeds 3,700 watts or its seat is under 26 inches high; the mini-motorcycle category for low seats covers only combustion engines under 50 cc. Before October 1, 2026 one of up to five brake horsepower (3,750 W) with a high seat was a motor-driven cycle
restrictions.citation: Connecticut General Statutes §14-1(59), (61), as amended by Public Act 26-24

restrictions.rule: Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement, which an applicant who hasn't held one in the past two years gets only after completing a novice motorcycle training course
A motorcycle instruction permit is available from age 16 and lasts 60 days; permit holders stay off multiple-lane limited-access highways and must wear a helmet
Riders and passengers under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218 (49 CFR 571.218); the age rose from 18 on October 1, 2025
Riders must wear goggles, glasses or a face shield unless it has a windshield or wind screen meeting DMV specifications
Registered and plated with the DMV, titled if under 20 model years old, and must carry insurance
Needs a DMV inspection before registration when it was never registered in Connecticut, wasn't bought from a Connecticut dealer, and its manufacturer isn't licensed in Connecticut

A seller who calls it an e-bike or electric bike must, before the sale and in every print or digital ad, state clearly and conspicuously in writing its classification under state law, or its likely one once modified as intended, and that it is a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws that insurance may not cover
One designed for unimproved terrain that the DMV finds unsuitable for highways and won't register is an all-terrain vehicle instead
